account_preferences:
    type: object
    description:
      Values of basic account preferences.

socket_type:
            type: number
          auth_method:
            type: number
          store_type:
            type: string
          login_at_startup:
            type: boolean
          check_new_mail:
            type: boolean
          check_time:
            type: number

Assert.deepEqual(
    accountPreferences.find(account => account.protocol === "pop3"),
    {
      protocol: "pop3",
      socket_type: Ci.nsMsgSocketType.plain,
      auth_method: Ci.nsMsgAuthMethod.passwordCleartext,
      store_type: "mbox",
      login_at_startup: false,
      check_new_mail: false,
      empty_trash_on_exit: false,
      download_on_biff: true,
      headers_only: false,
      leave_on_server: false,
    },

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: In this account metric, account_preferences in metrics.yaml becomes Glean.mail.accountPreferences in JavaScript, while object property keys such as socket_type and check_new_mail stay snake_case and match the schema. For this payload, keep those exact field names in the collector and deep-equality tests. This is a scoped generated-API naming pattern; it does not justify converting ordinary JavaScript properties to snake_case or renaming an existing generated metric. Source and tests were read but not compiled or run. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion remains pending.
title: Telemetry object keys and generated metric names occupy different naming layers
